title: Six known multiple-trigger bursts account for the one-day, two-degree GBM pair excess in 4418 selected triggers
abstract: We search a frozen Fermi GBM trigger table for repeated gamma-ray emission. We select 4418 GRB-class triggers from July 2008 to November 2026. We count pairs within four time limits from one hour to 30 days and three angle limits from 2 to 10 degrees. We compare the counts with 1999 position shuffles within each year and each month. Eight pairs within one day and two degrees belong to six known multiple-trigger bursts. Their catalog entries share precise positions. With one trigger per known event, the 12-cut excess test gives p=0.9280 for year shuffles and p=0.9685 for month shuffles. No new source is established. Shared positions are not independent confirmation. Coarse localizations, time-dependent exposure, and incomplete trigger selection limit the test. This is a catalog audit and a conditional null result, not a limit on the rate of repeating sources. Code, frozen data, source hashes, controls and figures are included.

display.caption: Pair counts before and after known event removal. Gray bands contain the central 95 percent of year-shuffled counts. The bands are pointwise, not simultaneous.
